biggest_gap.what: Engine._restoreFightFromSave() clears _equipLoadPinned, and game/src/save/fight.js persists fight.loadout.equip_load_pct which nothing ever reads back. A scenario that DECLARES its equip load therefore keeps it across a loadState() and loses it across a save. Round 3's new hands term (+9.5 kg for the default loadout) makes the recomputed answer land on the other side of the 30% cliff. Measured live, hostiles on the floor, nothing despawned: arena_duel with a shell-scale-hauberk and legion-greaves on reads 24.000000% / LIGHT / 26 i-frames / 22 f@60 recovery / 52 f@60 total before saveRoundTrip() and 33.424658% / MEDIUM / 22 i-frames / 34 recovery / 60 total after it. arena_flat gives the identical pair. Bare, arena_duel goes 24.000000% -> 13.013699%, same tier but still not the saved number. The counterfactual is round 3's OWN delete-the-fix switch: with __breakW116('hands') the same save and the same reload land at 20.410959%, LIGHT, 26 i-frames, so the hands term is exactly what crosses the cliff.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: arena_duel and arena_flat are the fixtures W1-09, W1-10 and W1-11 calibrate combat in, and round 3's stated safety argument is that those states pin their equip load so the calibration is `untouched, byte for byte`. That holds at load and fails after a save, so no equip-load-dependent measurement taken after a save/load anywhere in this project is trustworthy. From the player's chair it is worse and simpler: quit during a boss fight, resume, and your dodge is four frames shorter and 8 frames longer to recover from, with nothing having changed in the world. Seam S23 gives RI-CMB01 the i-frame count outright, and an in-fight number that changes across a reload is the one thing that ruling exists to protect. It is also RULES #7 verbatim — a field written into the save and never read back — and it is the shape round 3's own D4 probe was written to catch, missed because the probe loads 49 states and saves none.

remedy.action: 1. game/src/save/fight.js — persist the PIN and not only its value: write `equip_load_pinned: !!engine._equipLoadPinned` beside the existing `equip_load_pct`. 2. Engine._restoreFightFromSave() — restore both, and seed _equipLoadBase from the restored equipLoadPct the same way _buildCombat seeds it at engine.js:1104, so the first post-load engagement is a delta and not an assignment. A save that carries a pin comes back pinned; a save that does not comes back deriving, which is the behaviour round 2 verified and correctly praised. 3. Extend round 3's own D4 probe (tools/harness/w1-16-r3-live.mjs --probe states) to SAVE AND RELOAD each state and re-read the tier, not only load it — the check was written for exactly this question and cannot reach it. 4. Separately and smaller: give the equip-load spell effect its own offset field in sim/magic/apply.js instead of mutating combat.player.equipLoadPct, which removes the Math.max(0, ...) clamp asymmetry (Feather at 13.013699% currently leaves the caster at 42.833333% MEDIUM when it expires) and removes the need for the delta-origin state at the same time.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/harness/critic-w1-16-r3-live.mjs --probe pinfight reports states_whose_ROLL_TIER_changes_across_a_save_and_reload: [] and equip_load_moved_across_the_save: false on every pinned row — with the __breakW116('hands') counterfactual row still present and still unchanged, so the arm has not been made vacuous by removing the thing it compares against. node tools/harness/critic-w1-16-r3-offline.mjs stays at six PASS and --selftest still fails all six. node tools/harness/critic-w1-16-r3-live.mjs --probe antimerge still reports pack_left_the_roll_byte_identical: true, so the anti-merge has not been traded for the pin.

secondary_observations: sim/magic/apply.js loadHandler() clamps at zero on BOTH apply and undo — Math.max(0, pct + delta) and Math.max(0, pct - delta) — so Feather at any load below its magnitude leaves the caster HEAVIER when it expires. Round 3 found this and did not fix it, and measured only the cast half. Measured to its consequence here, live: 13.013699% LIGHT / 26 i-frames -> 0.000000% on cast -> 42.833333% MEDIUM / 22 i-frames after expiry. Engine._recomputeEquipLoad() carries the same clamp at engine.js:3980. The clean repair is to give the effect its own offset field rather than mutating the shared scalar.

RI-PRG07 §2's FOURTH TERM, `talismans`, has no slot, no weight column and no reader: the token appears in game/src only inside two comments quoting §2. Unlike fall_damage_mult it is not declared null in getBurden()'s equip_load_consumers table, so the census does not count it as missing. It is not hypothetical content — the build ships catalysts as first-class objects (game/data/magic/cast-classes.json `catalysts`, MagicSystem.setCatalyst, loadout.catalyst), RI-PRG07 §4 prices a talisman/catalyst at 3 kg, and S19 makes two-handing one a combat stance with its own hyperarmour rule.

The hands are in the equip ratio and in NEITHER burden term, against RI-PRG07 §3's `weight of ALL carried items, EQUIPPED OR NOT`. Measured: an ultra greatsword and a Naga tower move the equip load 13.013699% -> 45.205480% and leave burden at 0.000000 with carried_weight 0.0 kg. The same object also carries two weights at once — bog-iron-maul is 11.5 kg in carried.json (what burden weighs) and 16 kg as GHM in weapons/classes.json (what the roll weighs) — because round 3 correctly skips the pack row in §2 and _recomputeBurden() correctly counts it in §3.

The shipped shield and weapon weights contradict RI-PRG07 §4 at every comparable row: greatshield 12 vs 18, kite 5 vs 9, buckler 1.5 vs 4, straight sword 4 vs 6, dagger 1 vs 2, halberd 9 vs 12, greatsword 12 vs 14. Round 2's remedy asked for §4's numbers; round 3 used the shipped registries and invented nothing, which is the right instinct. But the ratio that decides the dodge is now computed from weights that disagree with the item that defines the ratio, and nobody has ruled which is authoritative. That is a corpus question, not a builder's guess.

engine.js:1099 calls the seeded _equipLoadBase `provably the bare equipment base with no effect offsets on it`. It is b.equipLoadPct at createPlayer, which for an unpinned state is the hardcoded 24.0 and has nothing to do with equipment. The arithmetic works because prev === pct at that instant, so the first engagement is a correct assignment rather than a delta. The comment will mislead the next reader.

The hist-sap-bow equip refusal is invisible to a player. Measured across the press: equip load 13.013699% before and after, weapon ssw_garrison_sword before and after, inventory slot null, HUD toast null, anything_the_player_could_see_changed FALSE. The reason exists on the equip_end event and nothing under game/src/ui or game/src/render reads equip_end or .refused; engine.uiToast() drives ui/hud.js's E11 element and is not called. The POLICY is right — guessing a bow would reproduce the round-2 defect — and the reason must not be piped verbatim, because it is a raw exception listing 87 internal weapon ids.

Engine.snapshot() and restoreState() are not a pair: snapshot() returns a trace record (makeRecord) and restoreState(blob) calls loadState(blob), which throws `expected a named state (string) or an elder-souls/save@1 blob`. Not a load path. Dropped from the pin ladder rather than counted as a throwing result.

CONFIRMED FIXED, not this piece's: W1-SAVE-AI closed the save/fight.js SKIP defect that omitted `ai`. Ten load paths measured with hostiles on the floor and nothing despawned; no path threw. saveRoundTrip() still reports hash_equal:false, and equip_load_pct is now one of its causes alongside death.last_grounded.

corpus_extended.what: Neither RI-PRG07 nor RI-CMB01 has a method that survives a save.
corpus_extended.detail: RI-PRG07 method 2 sweeps the breakpoints, method 3 asserts inventory does not move the roll, and RI-CMB01 M1 censuses the animation at each tier — all of them at load, in one session, with no persistence step anywhere. A build can pass every method in both items while a save and a reload silently re-tier the player, which is exactly what HEAD does. Suggested amendment for a corpus round: add to RI-CMB01 M1 `after the census, save and reload the state and re-take every row; assert byte-identical i-frame counts, windows and recovery`, and add to RI-PRG07 method 2 `assert the equip ratio is byte-identical across a save/load round trip on a state that declares its own equip load`. RULES #7 already says this in general terms; neither item's method implements it.

corpus_extended.what: RI-PRG07 §4's representative weights and the build's shipped weights disagree, and no ruling says which wins.
corpus_extended.detail: §4 declares Buckler 4 / Kite shield 9 / Greatshield 18 / Straight sword 6 / Greatsword 14; the build ships 1.5 / 5 / 12 / 4 / 12 across weapons/classes.json, weapons/offhand.json and combat/stamina.json. §4 is prose in a `Representative weights` table with no stated authority, and the shipped columns are what the running ratio reads. The gap matters because it is the difference between OVERLOADED being reachable by dressing and not: at §4's weights the heaviest legal set is 119 kg and OVERLOADED on both low sheets; at shipped weights it is 49.8 kg and HEAVY at best. Either §4 is the spec and the registries must be re-tuned to it, or §4 is illustrative and should say so.
